title: Lima beans and corn, cooked, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Lima beans (also called butter beans) and corn are a combination of legumes and grain that provides plant protein, fiber, and a range of vitamins. When cooked without added fat they retain their natural flavor and nutritional value.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Lima beans are among the largest beans, reaching 2–3 cm in length.
The corn used is typically sweet yellow or white, not the large‑kernel field varieties.
Lima beans contain more potassium than most other beans.
Combining legumes with corn gives a more complete amino‑acid profile, approaching a full protein.
Such mixtures have traditional roots in South America, where lima beans are a staple.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: The bean‑corn blend provides about 15 g of protein per 100 g of cooked product, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion, satiety, and helps regulate blood glucose levels.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Both ingredients supply thiamine, niacin, and folate, essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains iron and magnesium
items.content: Iron supports oxygen transport, while magnesium is important for muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The absence of added fat makes this dish suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans, including lima beans.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Beans contain phytic acid, which can reduce mineral absorption; soaking before cooking lowers its level.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Legumes can cause gastrointestinal gas in sensitive people; gradual introduction helps the gut adapt.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the beans and corn as a side dish, toss them into salads, soups, or use them as a base for grain bowls. They reheat well in the microwave or a non‑stick pan without oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cooked product in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3–4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 2 months, thawing in the fridge before use.
